## Overview

LRPLF01 is a **level-factors** model for word reading (`ewrswr`): what is associated
with the word-reading score *level* at each of the four timepoints (t1–t4),
modelled on the logit scale with a Beta-Binomial likelihood and a child random
intercept. Unlike the gain model it is **not autoregressive** — there is no own
baseline; per-timepoint intercepts absorb the maturation trend.

_Causal labelling + the level-model crossover caveat._ Under the revised study DAG (`dag/dag-language-reading.dagitty`, revised 2026-07-10)
every non-randomised coefficient is an **adjusted association** confounded by latent
general ability (the child random intercept is
only a partial, shrunken stand-in for between-child heterogeneity, not a control for
that latent general ability) — "associated with", never "drives". **Crucially,
the group effect is modelled as `group × time` — a per-timepoint group coefficient,
read as trajectory divergence — because after t2 the waitlist crosses over: the
group difference across the four timepoints is *not* a clean ITT contrast.** The
per-timepoint coefficient is parameterised as the covariate-adjusted arm gap at t1
(`arm_gap_t1`, a pre-randomisation *balance* quantity, never an effect) plus the
change in that gap at each later wave (`d_grp_time[t]`; #552). The clean randomised
contrast lives **only at t2** — the t2 change `d_grp_time[t2]`, a
difference-in-differences of adjusted levels, labelled *causal* in the table below;
the t3/t4 changes are randomised early-start-versus-delayed-start schedule
contrasts — not treated-versus-untreated effects, with no mechanistic reading — and
the per-wave gaps `b_grp_time[t] = arm_gap_t1 + d_grp_time[t]`
are kept as a derived levels view. SES is excluded (non-DAG / redundant).

**DAG factor set:** group $\times$ time · age (per timepoint) · cognitive ability
(block design) $\times$ time · group $\times$ ability · child random intercept.

## Model

$$
\operatorname{logit}\mu_{i,t} = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{time}[t]}
  + b_{\text{grp}[t]}\,\text{group}_i
  + \gamma_A A_{\text{std},t}
  + g_{\text{ability}[t]}\,z(\text{blocks})
  + \gamma_{\text{grp\_ability}}\,\text{group}_i\,z(\text{blocks})
  + u_{\text{child}[i]},
$$

with $W_t \sim \operatorname{BetaBinomial}(N, \mu\kappa, (1-\mu)\kappa)$, $N = 79$.
The per-timepoint group ($b_{\text{grp}[t]}$) and ability ($g_{\text{ability}[t]}$)
coefficients are the `group × time` and `ability × time` interactions; the clean
randomised contrast is the change in $b_{\text{grp}[t]}$ from t1 to t2 (see the
arm-gap parameterisation below). Priors follow the shared template in `priors.py`.

![Model diagram](model_graph.png){#fig-model .lightbox fig-align="left"}

**Arm-gap parameterisation (#552).** The per-timepoint group coefficient is centred on the timepoint-1 arm gap: $b_{\text{grp}[t1]} = a_{t1}$ and $b_{\text{grp}[t]} = a_{t1} + d_{\text{grp}[t]}$ for $t \in \{t2, t3, t4\}$, where $a_{t1}$ (`arm_gap_t1`) is the covariate-adjusted immediate-minus-waitlist gap at t1 — before anyone was treated, so a **chance balance quantity** on the cross-coupling prior, reported and never read as an effect — and $d_{\text{grp}[t]}$ (`d_grp_time[t]`) is the change in that gap from t1, on the outcome-tier treatment prior. A levels model conditions on nothing at baseline while adjusting for age and ability at every wave, so a free per-timepoint vector (the pre-#552 parameterisation, retained as the `arm_gap_reference="free"` comparator) carries the covariate-adjusted chance t1 imbalance straight into the t2 contrast; centring on the t1 gap removes it and puts the prior on the randomised difference directly. The randomised contrast is therefore the **t2 change `d_grp_time[t2]`**, a difference-in-differences of adjusted levels; `d_grp_time[t3]` / `[t4]` are randomised early-start-versus-delayed-start schedule contrasts — identified by the original randomisation but not treated-versus-untreated effects, with no mechanistic reading — and the per-wave arm gaps `b_grp_time[t]` are kept as a derived levels view.

**Intercepts (#389 finding 2).** $\alpha$ is **anchored**: a pooled, arm-blind
empirical-Bayes anchor at the observed **pre-randomisation t1** logit plus a free
zero-centred offset, and $\alpha_{\text{time}}$ is an exact **zero-sum**
wave-deviation vector. The previous parameterisation — a free global intercept and
four free per-timepoint offsets, all centred at logit zero — was identified only
through its sums (posterior correlations to $-0.96$) and implied prior-predictive
scores near half the instrument maximum for a population observed far below it.
The anchor uses only pre-randomisation data, so no treatment-affected quantity
enters the prior; the priors table labels the offset as empirical Bayes.
